options: A physical copy of all source systems held in a data warehouse
A virtual consumption layer that connects directly with many data stores
A technique for compressing data before it is stored
A backup process that snapshots databases nightly
A method of encrypting data in transit
questions.explanation: Data virtualization is a virtual consumption layer that connects directly with data stores such as RDBMS, data appliances, NoSQL, web services, SaaS and enterprise applications.

questions.stem: What happens to the data models of the source systems when data virtualization is used?
options: They are converted to a star schema
They are merged into a single physical table
They remain intact with no change
They are replaced by NoSQL documents
They are archived and rebuilt in the data lake
questions.explanation: Because the virtualization layer connects directly with all data stores, the data models of all systems remain intact with no change.

questions.stem: Data virtualization is described as one of the solutions for which problem statement?
options: Data sovereignty
Data compression
Data encryption
Data subsetting
Data scraping
questions.explanation: Data virtualization is considered one of the solutions for the data sovereignty problem statement, since data can stay where it is and be consumed virtually.

questions.stem: What does a data virtualization layer host in order to expose data?
options: Physical copies of every source table
Scheduled ETL jobs that move data nightly
Views connecting directly with the data stores, which may be one-to-one or complex SQL views
Encrypted archives of historical data
Cubes pre-aggregated for each department
questions.explanation: Data virtualization hosts views that connect directly with all possible data stores; these can be one-to-one views or complex SQL views pulling from multiple source systems.

questions.stem: What name is given to the second, third or fourth virtual data model layers built on top of the base virtualization layer?
options: Staging area
Virtual semantic layer
Operational data store
Data mart
Business vault
questions.explanation: Additional virtualized data models can be created as further layers to fulfil different business requirements, and all these layers can be called the virtual semantic layer.

questions.stem: In the data quality example, a data issue is found in three source systems and one data mart. What does data virtualization allow?
options: The issue is logged and each system owner fixes it separately
Only the data mart copy can be corrected
The four data stores are dropped and reloaded
The data in all four data stores can be fixed directly from the virtualization layer
The affected rows are hidden from the BI tool until IT resolves them
questions.explanation: Data virtualization has write-back capability, so data residing in the three source systems and the data mart can be fixed directly from the virtualization layer without separate implementation exercises.

questions.stem: A user wants one more column in a BI dashboard, but the pipeline from Data Lake to Data Warehouse to Data Marts to OLAP would take weeks or months. What solution does data virtualization offer?
options: Virtualize the source systems to get the column immediately, while IT processes the pipeline in parallel
Skip the data warehouse permanently and build the dashboard on the lake
Ask the user to wait until the next pipeline release
Hard-code the column value in the BI tool
Export the source table to a spreadsheet for the user
questions.explanation: The column is virtualized from the source and shown in the BI tool at once; once IT completes the pipeline, the virtual column is replaced with the pipelined one.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT an advantage claimed for data virtualization?
options: Single access point to all data stores
No additional storage is needed
Users write queries in one language and a wrapper talks to the connected systems
Historical data is maintained automatically
Write-back capability into source systems
questions.explanation: No historical data is a listed disadvantage: because no copy of the data is hosted, history is not maintained. The other four are listed advantages.

questions.stem: Why does data virtualization carry a performance impact as a disadvantage?
options: Because all data is duplicated into an in-memory cache
Because some queries run at the source systems
Because the semantic layer must be rebuilt after each query
Because ETL jobs compete for the same server
Because views are stored on slow disk
questions.explanation: The performance impact arises because some queries will run at the source, placing load on the source systems.

questions.stem: Alongside which data store is data virtualization said to be best suited?
options: A Kafka stream
A NoSQL database
A data warehouse already in place
A web scraping tool
A spreadsheet
questions.explanation: Data virtualization is best suited alongside a data warehouse in place, which supplies the history that virtualization alone does not keep.
